newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INSTANT VIEW - NZ c/a deficit worse than expected.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - NZ c/a deficit worse than expected.

text.p: Statistics New Zealand on Friday said New Zealand's current account deficit blew out to NZ$4.47 billion in the year to March 1997 -- the largest balance of payments deficit the country has ever recorded.
The deficit for the March quarter was $723 million. Economists had on average forecast a quarterly deficit of $212.2 million and an annual deficit of $4.1 billion.
The following are economists' initial reactions to the data.
JASON WONG, ECONOMIST AT FIRST NEW ZEALAND CAPITAL
"It's a bit worse than expected. Most of that was on the transfers balance, a falloff in migrants.
"I think all the risks lay on the downside anyway so I'm not particularly surprised."
He said next quarter the data would take account of the government's purchase of a naval frigate and that would take the balance to around 5.5 percent of GDP.
"These figures are not going to get any better in the near or medium-term."
The Reserve Bank was among the most pessimistic of forecasters.
"They won't react to it at all," Wong said.
"The dollar is showing signs of weakness and we have a negative view on the currency and we expect the current account figures is one of those many factors which will drive the currency lower."
